name: Behind-the-Back Barbell Wrist Curl
description: The behind-the-back wrist curl is performed standing with a barbell held behind the body in a pronated grip. The wrists curl upward against the barbell's weight, targeting the wrist flexors from an extended arm angle. This standing position can allow heavier loading than the seated version, and the neutral standing position eliminates upper arm fatigue from supporting the forearms.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding a barbell behind the body, hands in a pronated grip (overhand), bar resting at the level of the glutes.
execution.setup_instructions: Can grip from a rack at hip height behind the body, or take from a standard deadlift position.
steps: Step 1: Begin with the bar resting behind the thighs, wrists in slight extension.
Step 2: Curl the wrists upward by flexing the wrist joint, raising the back of the hands.
Step 3: Hold briefly at the top of wrist flexion.
Step 4: Lower the wrists back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Arms swinging forward — keep the bar behind the body
Flexing the elbows instead of just the wrists
safety_considerations: Use a grip that is comfortable — the behind-back position can stress the wrists
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full wrist extension to full flexion.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the forearms at the top
